title: Bretagne white car
description: White car (no antenna) in France is almost exclusively found in the region of Bretagne.

title: Slate roofs
description: The roofs made of slate are mainly situated in the Massif Central zone. You might find a few of them in very tiny zones in the Pyreneas and Manche.

title: French "cat" pylons
description: If you see an electric pylon looking like a cat (two ears and danders), you're 95% of times in France

title: Réunion car
description:
Réunion has a Street View car with visible side mirrors, a roof rack, and black tape at the end of the rear right bar.

NOTE: Make sure not to get this confused with the Ghana car, which has tape on the front right bar.

title: French infrastructures
description: Being a French Department, you will see French infrastructure, such as signs, bollards and poles.

title: Réunion landscape
description: Réunion is a mountainous volcanic island in the Indian Ocean on a similar latitude to Queensland, Australia. Most roads are along the coast, with lush green mountains visible close by. Vegetation consists of palms and ferns, pine trees at higher elevation, and flowering plants due to the island’s tropical savanna climate.

title: Réunion bus stops
description:
There are six distinct bus stop designs on Réunion
This infographic shows where each one can be found. The list above is ranked by how common each one is found.

title: Sugarcane
description: Sugarcane plantations on Réunion can be found in two regions: the northeast and the southwest. The southwest is generally more built up and densely populated, meaning you will see more buildings or cars around.

title: Cilaos
description: Cilaos is a town inside a caldera. It can be recognized by the wall of mountains surrounding the town with overcast coverage.

title: Saint Louis blur
description: You can spot this rectangular blur on the front camera in all the coverage going north of Saint-Louis.

title: North East N1
description:
The northwestern section of the N1 is divided, with a distinct ridge to the southeast and the ocean to the northwest.
Note that although a bridge appears on the map, the coverage was taken before the bridge was built, meaning you will not see the bridge.

title: Volcano Road
description: Route du Volcan can be recognized by the Martian landscape. The only vegetation is scattered shrubs and the soil is a distinct brown-red colour. These white stones lining the road are also a good clue.

title: Route Forestière 58
description: La Route Forestière 58 de la Scierie et du Haut des Makes is a winding dirt track that can be recognized by the dense vegetation surrounding it, particularly pine trees and eucalyptus. The track itself is also dark in colour, with grass growing in the middle of it.

title: East
description: The eastern region of Réunion is the least densely populated, evident by the eastern part of the N2, which is a single carriageway passing through somewhat dense vegetation on both sides, or a vast landscape with little to no trees.

title: Saint Paul & Saint Denis bollards
description: The two largest towns in Réunion can be differentiated by their bollards, commonly seen at intersections. Saint Paul uses black bollards, while Saint Denis uses green bollards, often with white balls on top. Saint Denis is also more built up, being the capital.

title: Périgord yellow limestone
description: In Périgord, a lot of buildings are made using the local limestone with a very distinct yellow tint.

title: France - Landscape : Millevaches
description: Easily recognizable landscape : Douglas fields (Pseudotsuga menziesii) + broom everywhere + Pteridium aquilinum. Difference with similar region : The broom everywhere rules out the Morvan region + absence of hedgerows/Charolais cattle - The Douglas fir rules out the Périgord region)

title: France - Architcture : Ferme Bressane
description: The Bresse farmhouse is characterized by its long, narrow main building. Now renovated into residential homes, they line the roads of the region. The walls are made of brick with wooden frames (not always visible).

title: France - Architecture : Ardoise des Pyrénées
description: A high mountain landscape with slate...You are probably in the valleys of the central Pyrenees!

title: France - Architecture : Bergerie du Cantal
description: Slate or stone slabs, low facade topped by a high sloping roof.

title: France - Architecture : Bordelais
description: Large, well-cut limestone blocks, on houses no more than 2 stories high. Typical of the 18th century.

title: France - Architecture : Calcaire jaune de l'Argonne
description: On the Ardennes/Marne border: the characteristic yellow stone of the region is associated with the red brick wall with roofs mostly made of tile (presence of slate).

title: France - Architecture : Clocher comtois
description:
Bell tower topped with a dome. Iron or glazed tile. 18th century.

(sur 665 clochers répertoriés en 1980 sur le territoire franc-comtois, 277 Haute-Saône, 257 Doubs, 124 Jura, 7 Territoire de Belfort)

title: France - Architecture : Clunisois et Mâconais
description: Architecture of Saône et Loire departement with round (canal) tiles.

title: Est Pays-Basque
description: The architecture of the Basque Country is easily recognizable. To be even more precise, slate roofs are found to the east of Saint-Palais, while to the west, canal tiles are used.

title: Ferme Beauceronne
description:
Hamlet farm, large farmhouse, fortified farm...

The large estates of the Paris Basin are easily recognizable. Buildings dating from the 18th century, when the Physiocrats reigned supreme; or from the 19th century, with the organization of agricultural production modeled on capitalist industry. Nothing better for turning wheat into hard cash.

Beauce = Strong presence of slate roofs

title: France - Architecture : Ferme Chalosse
description: Landes farmhouse with double-pitched roof. + some walls made of stone or pebbles.

title: Galets
description: These types of walls can be found: Rhône Valley between Lyon and Avignon Isère and Durance Valleys Valleys of the major rivers flowing down from the Pyrenees.

title: Grande ferme de la Brie
description:
Hamlet farm, large farmhouse, fortified farm...

The large estates of the Paris Basin are easily recognizable. Buildings dating from the 18th century, when the Physiocrats reigned supreme; or from the 19th century, when agricultural production was organized according to the capitalist industrial model. Nothing better for turning wheat into hard cash.

In Brie, flat tiles are predominant, but slate is also present. Window frames and decorative elements are sometimes made of brick.

title: Haute-Normandie
description:
In Upper Normandy, the combination of slate, half-timbering, and brick is particularly common.
To the south, brick walls become less frequent, and to the north, slate disappears, giving way to modern mixed black and red tiles.

(This pattern has been observed from the north of the Orne department to the south of Dieppe).

title: Middle of France
description:
From western Burgundy to the south of the Eure and Orne departments, roofs are composed in equal parts of flat, modern tiles and slate (more slate is found along the Loire Valley). Wall frames and gateways are often made of brick.

Useful for refining a guess by eliminating nearby regions: The absence of curved tiles eliminates Charente/Vendée; the presence of flat tiles, the Pays de la Loire region; brick and slate, Burgundy (except for the Morvan).

title: Lauze de schiste des Pyrénées
description: While Pyrenean slate is well-known, did you know that its coarser version, lauze, is found only in a few isolated valleys? Vicdessos Valley, upper Aude Valley...

title: Maison landaise
Architecture : Nord (Avesnois)
description: Full Slate + Red Brick = On the North South axis: Maubeuge / Laon; East-West Charleville / Saint Quentin.

title: Architecture : Nord et Pas-de-Calais
description: North of Arras, between the Escault and Opal Coast parks, slate becomes rare. It is replaced by black tiles, resulting in a strong contrast between modern black and red tiles. South of this area and to the west (Avesnois), slate is much more prevalent.

title: Architecture : Nord - bricks walls + limestones
description: If North of France and presence of limestone, 2 possible zones: Opal marsh (only red tile -except upper building / West of Laon

title: Architecture : West Basque Country
description: The architecture of the Basque Country is easily recognizable. To be even more precise, slate roofs are found to the east of Saint-Palais, while to the west, canal tiles are used.

title: Architecture : Pierre de Champlitte
description: The walls and low walls located between Champlitte, Gray, and Vesoul are built using thin, flat limestone blocks dating from the Jurassic period. Unlike the thick limestone typical of Burgundy, these structures are found in Haute-Saône and Haute-Marne, primarily along the Saône and Ognon valleys. They are also found to the west of this area, in the Châtillonnais region and along the Seine basin.

title: Architecture : Poitou-Charentes + Vendée
description:
South of the lower Loire Valley, as far south as La Rochelle and as far east as Poitiers: alternating patterns of terracotta "canal" tiles and slate.

(Slate is more commonly found on manor houses, while terracotta tiles are more common on modern, single-story houses.)

title: Architecture : Somme, Nord et Pas-de-Calais.
description: Between Amiens, Arras, and Cambrai, one finds an alternation of slate and tile roofs with walls entirely made of brick. Further north, the slate disappears, replaced by modern black tiles; further south, the brick walls vanish, only the window and door frames remain.

title: Architecture : Sud touraine
description: South of Tours, you can find these particular roofs with flat tiles and slate on the same slope.

title: Architecture : Toulousaine
description: Bricks and canal tiles: welcome to Toulouse.

title: Architecture : Tiles canal of Bresse
description: In eastern France, excluding Lorraine/Moselle, "canal tile" roofs appear in Bresse south of Cuisery (with rare exceptions). With a flat, damp, bocage landscape and extensive corn cultivation, a 4900 is guaranteed!

title: Architecture : Canal Tiles of Lorraine
description: This enclave of Mediterranean-style roofs in Lorraine is marked by the following locations, starting from its northern tip: Varennes-en-Argonne, east of Châlons-en-Champagne, Brienne-le-Château, Bar-sur-Aube, north of Chaumont, Épinal, Gerbéviller, north-east of Nancy and Metz, and north of Verdun

title: Glazed Tiles
description: Cistercian style. Bourgogne-Franche-comté

title: Beet fields
description: Beet fields : filthy, lifeless, soulless. A vile monoculture in northern France and the Champagne region. Imagine the money the agrochemical companies and the beneficiaries of land consolidation have made since the 1960s.

title: Clementine
description: Especially in the Northeast plain of Corse

title: Douglas
description: Douglas Field Dangling cones

title: Fruit trees
description: Fruit growing areas are quite limited and useful to learn about.
